record.paper_title: Problems and Conjectures in Matrix and Operator Inequalities
record.original_question: Let λ_1,…,λ_n lie in the closed unit disk, define D=diag(λ_1-λ_n,…,λ_{n-1}-λ_n), and let J be the all-ones matrix of size n-1. Must the matrix D(I-J/n) always have at least one eigenvalue in the closed unit disk? This is presented as a reformulation of Sendov's conjecture.

evidence.quote:
Conjecture 11 Let D = diag(λ1 −λn, . . . , λn−1 −λn), where λ1, . . . , λn belong
to the closed unit disk. Then D(I − J/n) has an eigenvalue in the closed unit
disk.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer and let $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \ldots, \lambda_n$ be complex numbers lying in the closed unit disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \leq 1\}$. Define the $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ diagonal matrix
$$D = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_n,\ \lambda_2 - \lambda_n,\ \ldots,\ \lambda_{n-1} - \lambda_n),$$
and let $J$ denote the $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ matrix all of whose entries equal $1$, with $I$ the $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ identity matrix. Prove or disprove: the matrix
$$D\left(I - \tfrac{1}{n} J\right)$$
always has at least one eigenvalue lying in the closed unit disk.

(Equivalently, this asserts that for every monic polynomial of degree $n$ with all roots $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n$ in the closed unit disk, every root $\lambda_k$ has at least one critical point of the polynomial within distance $1$ from it.)
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is a matrix reformulation of Sendov's conjecture. It is known to hold for degrees n ≤ 8 (Brown, Borcea, and others), and Terence Tao (2020, published in Acta Mathematica 2022) proved it for all sufficiently large n. The full conjecture remains open for the intermediate range of degrees. A 2022 arXiv preprint by Dimitrov claiming a complete proof has not been broadly accepted/verified.

status_evidence.title: Sendov's conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture is known for n ≤ 8 (Brown, Borcea) and for sufficiently large n (Tao).
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is verified for low degrees and asymptotically, but not in general.

status_evidence.title: Sendov's conjecture for sufficiently high degree polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Tao proves Sendov's conjecture for n sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic resolution of Sendov's conjecture by Tao.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the Sendov conjecture for polynomials of degree at most eight
status_evidence.snippet: Sendov's conjecture is established for polynomials of degree at most 8.
status_evidence.claim: Low-degree cases up to n=8 are settled.
